title: A bitmap allocator
description:
Operating systems, file systems and game engines hand out fixed-size slots (pages, disk blocks, particles) from a **bitmap**: one bit per slot, 1 meaning used. Build one in assembly, using the bit instructions from lesson 7.05, a `struc` for its header (lesson 7.04) and a macro (lesson 7.02).

The allocator lives in memory the caller provides, laid out as:

```nasm
struc pool
    .count:  resq 1          ; how many slots there are (at most 64 * 4 = 256)
    .used:   resq 1          ; how many are in use
    .bits:   resq 4          ; the bitmap: bit i of the whole 256-bit field is slot i
endstruc
```

Write these functions (the tests pass the pool as an array of six qwords):

| Function | Effect | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `pool_init(pool, count)` | sets count, clears used and every bit | count, or −1 if count is 0 or more than 256 (and then changes nothing) |
| `pool_alloc(pool)` | finds the **lowest** free slot, marks it used | the slot number, or −1 if all are used |
| `pool_free(pool, slot)` | marks the slot free | 1 if it was in use, 0 if it was already free or out of range |
| `pool_is_used(pool, slot)` | | 1 or 0 (0 when out of range) |
| `pool_count_used(pool)` | counts the 1 bits with `popcnt` | the number of used slots |

    .used:   resq 1
    .bits:   resq 4
endstruc

        ret

        ret

solution.solution.asm:
struc pool
    .count:  resq 1
    .used:   resq 1
    .bits:   resq 4
endstruc

; IN_RANGE slot_register, label: jumps to label when the slot is not below pool.count (rdi = the pool).
%macro IN_RANGE 2
        cmp     %1, [rdi + pool.count]
        jae     %2
%endmacro

pool_init:
        mov     rax, -1
        test    rsi, rsi
        jz      .done
        cmp     rsi, 256
        ja      .done
        mov     [rdi + pool.count], rsi
        mov     qword [rdi + pool.used], 0
%assign q 0
%rep 4
        mov     qword [rdi + pool.bits + q * 8], 0
%assign q q + 1
%endrep
        mov     rax, rsi
.done:  ret

pool_alloc:
        xor     ecx, ecx                ; which qword of the bitmap
.next:  cmp     rcx, 4
        jae     .full
        mov     rax, [rdi + pool.bits + rcx*8]
        not     rax                     ; free slots are now 1 bits
        test    rax, rax
        jz      .try_next
        tzcnt   rax, rax                ; the lowest free bit in this qword
        mov     rdx, rcx
        shl     rdx, 6
        add     rdx, rax                ; the slot number
        IN_RANGE rdx, .full             ; past the last slot: everything usable is taken
        bts     [rdi + pool.bits + rcx*8], rax
        inc     qword [rdi + pool.used]
        mov     rax, rdx
        ret
.try_next:
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .next
.full:  mov     rax, -1
        ret

pool_free:
        xor     eax, eax
        IN_RANGE rsi, .done
        mov     rcx, rsi
        shr     rcx, 6                  ; the qword
        and     esi, 63                 ; the bit inside it
        btr     [rdi + pool.bits + rcx*8], rsi
        jnc     .done                   ; it was already free
        dec     qword [rdi + pool.used]
        mov     eax, 1
.done:  ret

pool_is_used:
        xor     eax, eax
        IN_RANGE rsi, .done
        mov     rcx, rsi
        shr     rcx, 6
        and     esi, 63
        bt      [rdi + pool.bits + rcx*8], rsi
        setc    al
.done:  ret

pool_count_used:
        xor     eax, eax
%assign q 0
%rep 4
        popcnt  rcx, [rdi + pool.bits + q * 8]
        add     rax, rcx
%assign q q + 1
%endrep
        ret

hints: Slot n is bit `n mod 64` of qword `n / 64`: `shr` by 6 and `and` with 63 split a slot number into those two parts, and the qword is at `[rdi + pool.bits + qword*8]`.
To find a free slot, invert a qword with `not`: the free slots become 1 bits, and `tzcnt` gives the lowest one. A qword of all ones (every slot used) inverts to 0: move on to the next.
`btr` copies the old bit into the carry flag before clearing it, so `jnc` tells you the slot was already free. `bt` plus `setc al` turns a bit into 0 or 1.
requirements: Field offsets come from the `pool` struc, never raw numbers.
`pool_alloc` finds a free slot with `tzcnt` (or `bsf`) on the inverted qword, not by testing bit after bit.
`used` always matches the number of 1 bits.
stretch: Allocate a run of n neighbouring slots, and a thread-safe version with `lock bts` and `lock btr`.
rules: Reach the bitmap through the struc field pool.bits.
Find the free slot with tzcnt or bsf.
Count the used slots with popcnt.
